name: Silodosin
sections: White to pale yellowish-white powder, very slightly soluble in water.

The most alpha-1A-selective alpha-blocker available, giving minimal blood-pressure effects but a high rate of ejaculatory dysfunction. First approval/introduction: Japan 2006 (Kissei Pharmaceutical / Daiichi Sankyo); US FDA 2008; EU 2010.

Highly selective blockade of alpha-1A receptors in the prostate, bladder neck and prostatic urethra relaxes smooth muscle, improving urine flow and lower urinary tract symptoms with minimal effect on blood pressure. Receptor / target profile: Alpha-1A antagonist with ~162-fold selectivity over alpha-1B and ~50-fold over alpha-1D receptors.
Hepatic – UGT2B7 glucuronidation (active KMD-3213G), CYP3A4, ADH/ALDH
Summary: Bioavailability ~32%; Tmax ~2.6 h (take with food). ~97% protein bound. Metabolised by UGT2B7, CYP3A4 and ADH. Half-life ~13 h.
